RoomType.rationale: FrogKnightNormal.cs:9 `RoomType => RoomType.Monster`. Modeled structurally by pool membership. One shared mechanism across this batch; see `encounter/_room_type_and_weak` in the report.

AllPossibleMonsters.issue: FrogKnightNormal.cs:11 returns a single-element list with `FrogKnight`. Shared finding, filed once under `encounter/_all_possible_monsters` (see `encounter/aeonglass` for the full enumeration; dormant).

GenerateMonsters.rationale: ROSTER: FrogKnightNormal.cs:13-16 returns exactly one `(FrogKnight, null)` pair; `FROG_KNIGHT_NORMAL = Encounter(id="frog_knight_normal", monster_classes=[FrogKnight])` (frog_knight.py:97-100) -- one monster, same class. ORDER: trivially matches. SLOT: C# passes `null`; the sim's `monster_slots` default `()` leaves `slot_name=None` too -- matches. DRAW COUNT: zero on both sides -- `FrogKnightNormal.GenerateMonsters` never touches `base.Rng`, and the sim's fixed-composition path draws nothing (monsters/base.py:477-479, `create_monsters`'s own comment).

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: `EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false` (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden. The sim's `Encounter` dataclass is never registered with `HookSystem` -- never a hook listener on either side.

FrogKnightNormal overrides neither Min/MaxGoldReward (inherits `RoomType.Monster`'s 10-20, matching `GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]`, rewards.py:171) nor ShouldGiveRewards (default `true`/`True` on both sides). `FROG_KNIGHT_NORMAL` passes none of `min_gold`/`max_gold`/`should_give_rewards` (frog_knight.py:97-100).
